title: Open Road
intro: This is the base that gets your legs back between points. You get about twenty-five seconds, and your body spends them recovering on oxygen. That's the engine this session builds. It needs shoes and a bit of flat road, nothing else, so it fits into almost any week.

Run for twenty-eight minutes at one pace. You should be able to say a full sentence out loud the whole way. If you can't, slow down. Harder than that and it stops being this session, so no surges and no fast finish. Running puts braking through your legs, and court days give you plenty already. In a heavy court week, do Engine Builder on the bike instead. If a shin, foot, ankle or knee is sore right now, ride a bike or walk today and get it looked at. Stop the session and get it checked if you get a sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, or a joint that gives way. Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right means stop now and get it looked at before you train again. If a doctor has told you to be careful with hard exercise, check with them before you do this one.

good: Walk fast enough that your arms swing, and look ahead
Feel your legs waking up and your breathing lift a little
Drive the knee forward over your toes
Feel the stretch low in the calf and the front of the ankle
bad: Letting the heel lift or the arch collapse

good: Step forward onto a straight leg and reach both hands toward your toes
Feel the back of the front thigh stretch
bad: Rounding your back instead of hinging at the hip

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor with Overhead Reach

good: Squeeze the back glute, then reach the same-side arm overhead
Feel it at the front of the back hip
bad: Arching your lower back to feel more

good: Hold a wall and swing the leg front to back, then side to side
The swing should get a little bigger every rep
bad: Arching your lower back to throw the leg higher

good: Rise onto the ball of your foot, pause, then lower slowly
Squeeze the calf at the top
Jog a little faster every minute until you reach your run pace
Feel your stride settle and your breathing find a rhythm

exercises.name: Easy Run
exercises.note: If you don't run already, run two minutes and walk one the whole way instead.

good: Pick a flat loop you can repeat and hold one pace the whole way
Feel your breathing stay smooth and your shoulders and hands stay loose
bad: Speeding up because it starts to feel easy

good: Walk slowly with your arms hanging loose
Feel your heart rate come down with every step
bad: Standing still the second the run ends

good: Press the back heel into the floor and lean your hips toward a wall
Feel it in the upper part of the calf
bad: Letting the back heel lift off the floor
